subject: Mark-recapture using dCJS: logProb is NA or NaN

messages.author: e294dd6d325c0bfa
messages.subject: Mark-recapture using dCJS: logProb is NA or NaN
parts:
Hi folks,
 After spending most of the day failing to see a solution to this, I'd appreciate any insights others may have. I have a fairly unexcptional capture history matrix (ch) of around 6000 birds marked at 100 or sites, and I'd like to estimate their survival (eventually using a CAR-type model, but I need to get the basics first!) I should also say the data and (full) model work in BUGS and in Nimble specifying the likelihoods directly, but I'd like to speed it up using the dCJS feature.

 My problem is that using dCJS I get:
warning: logProb of data node ch[131, 3:17]: logProb is NA or NaN.

for each of the nodes, and I can't for the life of me spot why, although I am 99% sure I'm just being dim. I've tried to simplify the model as far as I can, but still get the same messages, so I'm guessing it's something fairly fundamental I'm missing. Suggestions please!

The model code is below, it's cut down from the fuller model, hence the idiosyncratic phrasing. FWIW, I'm running nimble 0.10.0 and nimbleEcology 0.3.1 in R 4.0.0 in Windows. 

Many thanks in advance for any insights
Rob

code <- nimbleCode({

for (s in 1:n.site){
  for (t in 1:(n.occ-1)){
    phi[t, s] <- 1 / (1 + exp(-lphi[t, s]))    # survival
    p[t, s] <- 1 / (1 + exp(-lp[t, s]))        # recapture
    lphi[t, s] <- mu.lphi
    lp[t, s] <- mu.lp
  }
}

mu.lphi ~ dnorm(0, 0.1)
mu.lp ~ dnorm(0, 0.1)

for( i in 1:n.ch ){
ch[i, first[i]:last[i]] ~ dCJS_vv(probSurvive = phi[first[i]:last[i], site[i]], 
    probCapture = p[first[i]:last[i], site[i]],
    len = last[i]-first[i]+1)
        # first[] is the time of first capture, and last[] the last capture occasion (for now)
}
})

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Mark-recapture using dCJS: logProb is NA or NaN
parts:
Hi Rob,

What do you see when you build the model and try inspecting its values?

model <- nimbleModel(<your args>)

model$ch[131, 3:17]

Often initial values are an issue.  Did you set reasonable inits for mu.lp and mu.lphi?  You can look with

model$phi
model$p

BTW, there is an expit function.

It looks like you may be setting up to elaborate with time- or site-specific explanatory pieces, but if not you can vectorize:

phi[1:(n.occ-1), s] <- expit(lphi[ 1:(n.occ-1), s]))

If you're still stuck, we can look more if you are able to send a reproducible example with some data (off-list if you prefer not to post the data publicly, but maybe only a few sites of data would be sufficient?).

Best,
-Perry

messages.author: 9b1f1220a2b07d1e
messages.subject: Re: Mark-recapture using dCJS: logProb is NA or NaN
parts:
Hi Rob et al.,

It jumps out at me that detection probability at the n.occ-th detection survey aren't being calculated, but are needed by dCJS_vv if last[i] ever equals n.occ.  Since dCJS conditions on first capture, I think p[first[i]] is ignored, but p[last[i]] needs to be not NA. Since you're only calculating for t in 1:(n.occ - 1), and surveys during the n.occ-th period will have p = NA unless you're directly initializing p. Is that relevant?

Ben

messages.subject: Re: Mark-recapture using dCJS: logProb is NA or NaN
parts:
Ben,
 Thanks for that - if we ever meet in a bar, there's definitely a drink with your name on it :) That seems to be exactly the problem - and I would never have thought of that. model$p[ , 1] does indeed say that the last value is NA. Coming from a tradition of writing out the likelihood, I guess I'm used to implicitly shifting the p matrix so that both it and phi have the same length but offset. So that's a really useful insight, in the absence of a bar please accept a large amount of gratitude.

Perry,
 Thanks for the tips, they'll certainly be helpful for debugging!

Cheers both, and fingers crossed for a good outcome tonight - I'm watching from afar...
Rob
